name: Watercolor Storybook
summary: Transparent watercolour washes and loose, broken ink lines on warm cold-pressed paper: a living illustrated fairy-tale book.
description: The whole image reads as a page from an illustrated children's book. The ground is a per-pixel pigment simulation over cream paper (absorbance mixing, pooled wash edges, bare-paper gaps, granulation, lifted light pools) with composed regions: meadows with drifts of flowers, ponds rimmed by reeds, forests of tiered storybook trees with sunlit clearings, winding dirt paths. Characters and props are layered washes with wet-in-wet blooms and a misregistered, tapered sepia ink contour broken in 2-3 places; they move on painted held poses (8-pose walk, breathing idle, squash-and-lift hits, bleeding dissolves). A deckled bare-paper margin frames the screen like a book page.
avoidFor: projects that need hundreds of unique animated sprites generated at runtime

difficulty.why: Every new asset is assembled from hand-tuned wash shapes (base + 2-3 wet-in-wet blobs + highlight + pooled rim) and broken ink contours, posed by a small rig and baked per pose (15-19 frames for a main character); trees need a silhouette wash plus clipped glaze tiers. It takes several iterations per asset to read as painted, and the bake makes the style take 1-3 s to load.

technique.resolution: Native resolution, smooth scaling. Sprites baked at 3 px per world unit (collectibles 4, small FX 4-6); ground chunks rendered per pixel at up to 2.5 px per world unit (256-unit chunks).
technique.summary: Every colour is laid down as a transparent wash: per pixel in absorbance space (paper * exp(-absorbance)) for the ground, or on a scratch canvas (fill + blurred blobs + pooled rim + grain multiply, clipped, optionally multiplied as a glaze) for sprites, then overlaid with tapered sepia ink lines offset from the wash by ~0.45/0.35 units. Poses come from small rigs (body bob, head lag, planted feet, counter-swinging hands, trailing scarf and leaves) and are baked once.
technique.linework: Sepia ink #2a1b14 (blue-black #252c46 for ghost creatures and forest grass). Lines are filled ribbons, not strokes: width 0.7-0.95 units for body contours, 1.5 for the large creature, 0.3-0.45 for details; tapered at both ends (first 12-30 %, last 16-40 %), pressure wobble 0.6*sin(s*0.8)+0.4*sin(s*2.1) at 30 %, thicker on the side away from the upper-left light (light factor 0.45-0.6). Contours are broken into 2-3 pieces with small overshoots; tree crowns and many props are inked only on the shade side. Round caps and joins.
technique.shading: Wet-in-wet: blurred ellipses of lighter (top-left) and darker (bottom-right) pigment inside each shape (blur 0.5-2.6 units, alpha 0.4-0.95), a radial paper-white highlight at 30 %/26 % of the bbox, and a blurred darker rim (1-1.8 units, alpha 0.5-0.65) for pigment pooling. Tree foliage is built as glazes: one light crown wash, then 3 multiply tiers (45-50 % alpha) with hard scalloped top edges, darker and higher on the shade side, clipped to the crown. Hatching only on boulders and the large creature.
technique.lighting: Light from the upper left (direction -0.6, -0.8). Shadows are one shared indigo glaze rgba(50,54,92,0.2) per frame (union Path2D), lighter 0.11 for floating creatures. Carved faces, cracks and lanterns glow with warm yellow washes plus an additive radial glow sprite (alpha ~0.3, flickering). Forest floors warm to sap green #acb880 where light falls through the canopy.
technique.texture: Cold-pressed paper tooth, pigment granulation (multiplied grain canvas), wash-flow noise for edges, lifted (wiped) light pools with a darker tide line, backrun bloom rings and sparse pigment splatter baked into the ground; deckled bare-paper page margin on screen.

paletteRules: The paper is always the lightest value; never use pure white #ffffff except tiny specular dots (rgba 255,253,244).
Ground stays mid-light and low-chroma (meadow largest, then forest floor, golden fields, paths ~10 %, ponds a few %) so the saturated characters (pumpkin orange, violet, indigo) pop.
Mix ground colours in absorbance space (subtractive), not by alpha-blending RGB: overlapping washes get darker and richer, never greyer.
Every shape has a lighter top-left and darker bottom-right pigment blob of a neighbouring hue (orange -> yellow-ochre / burnt sienna, violet -> lilac / plum).
Trees use 4 autumn triplets (light / mid / accent) plus a dark edge at 50-62 % of the mid colour; foliage tiers are glazed with multiply, never painted opaque.
Ink is warm sepia #2a1b14, never pure black; cold subjects (ghost creatures, forest grass) switch to blue-black #252c46.
Shadows are indigo glazes (50,54,92), never black or grey.

typography.role: Titles, clock, big numbers, card names (old book small caps)
typography.css: font: 400 40px/1 'IM Fell English SC', 'IM Fell English', Georgia, serif; letter-spacing: 1.5px; color: #2a1b14;
font: italic 600 18px/1.2 'Cormorant Garamond', Georgia, serif; color: #5b3a24;

typography.role: Handwritten labels, small tags, floating counters, key hints

world.summary: A per-pixel watercolour shader paints terrain washes (meadow, forest floor, golden field, dirt path, ponds) over paper in absorbance space, with pooled dark edges, bare-paper gaps, granulation and lifted light pools; composed decals follow the regions (reeds and lily pads on pond banks, leaf litter and roots under every tree, flower drifts in meadows, stones on paths). Everything is baked into 256-unit chunks.
layers: Paper base #f5eede modulated by paper tooth (0.95 + 0.075 * noise)

Terrain washes from domain-warped fbm fields (forest scale 820, field 640, ponds 300, path 560 units) with signed-distance edges perturbed by flow noise (edge softness 0.45-5.45 units in wet-in-wet zones); pixels more than ~10 units from every edge take an exact fast path

Edge pooling (density up to x1.85 within 2.6 units inside an edge), 0.75-unit paper gaps between washes and a reserved white line around ponds; ponds go from shallows #b0cccc to deep #6a84aa with streak glints and a muddy bank band #cebe96
Lifted light pools from a low-frequency field (density -34 % meadow, -38 % forest) with a darker tide line; in forests they warm to sap green #acb880 (light through the canopy)

Decals in clusters, never sprinkled: backrun blooms (r 5-16), grass tufts in clumps and along paths and banks, one flower species per 210-unit drift, leaf litter in the tree colours under each tree (shadow side) with roots and mushrooms, fir needles and cones, lily pads near banks, stones on paths, stubble rows in fields

characters.summary: Characters are assembled from wash shapes + broken ink contours, posed by small rigs and baked once per pose: the main character has an 8-pose walk (contact - down - passing - up, twice), 6 breathing idles, a blink, a glance, a dash crouch, a dash stretch and a flinch; creatures have 6-pose cycles plus a hit pose, and every creature gets baked dissolve and soft (spawn) frames. The main character is a pumpkin-headed child in an indigo coat and trailing red scarf, ~18 units wide and ~30 tall (head rx 8.5, ry 6.9). Creatures: a small violet-crowned root creature with a leafy top (r 9, two colourings), a fast frosty floating sheet with a rippling hem (r 7, 90 % alpha) and a large cracked umber root creature with glowing seams (r 17).
rules: Big round head (about half the height), small body, stubby legs: storybook proportions with one characterful feature each (carved glowing face, leaf crown, rippling hem, glowing cracks).
Each part = wash (base + 2-3 wet-in-wet blobs + highlight + rim + granulation) followed by a 2-3 piece broken ink outline; back limbs first, front arm last.

Rig rules: body lowest just after contact, head settles a beat later (overlap), feet stay planted while the hips ride, hands counter-swing, scarf tail, leaves and hem trail as a travelling wave (follow-through).
Faces are carved glowing shapes or ink dots with heavy tapered brows; the glow sprite follows the baked head position of every frame.
The ink contour is thicker on the shadow side (bottom-right), so silhouettes read against the busy ground.
Crowds never move in lock-step: each creature starts its cycle at a seed-based phase and has its own scale (0.93-1.07) and breathing rate.
Every actor stands on an indigo glaze shadow ellipse (main character 7.6 x 2.8 units, creatures r*0.95 x r*0.36; the shadow grows in with the spawn).
Hit = the hit pose (eyes squeezed, mouth open, leaves flung) squashed 12 % against the knock for 140 ms while the pigment lifts to paper white; death = freeze, slump, bleed out into a puddle.

props.summary: 28 prop sprites baked once with the same wash + broken-outline toolkit, mirrored by flipping: four designed deciduous trees (broad oak, tall poplar, leaning two-mass, young sparse; 72x102 units), two firs (5 zigzag tiers), three bushes, three reed clumps with cattails, pumpkins (orange, amber, cream, carved and glowing), haystacks, fences, dry-stone walls, a signpost, a scarecrow and paired boulders. Placement follows the world: trees dense inside forests (two jittered grids, mostly firs deep inside), bushes along forest edges and pond banks, reeds in clumps on banks, boulders paired near paths and water, fences in meadow runs.
rules: Same light as everything else: lighter wash top-left, darker glazes and an indigo multiply glaze bottom-right, ink on the shade side.

Trees: the trunk forks below the crown (Y silhouette); the crown = union of 6-8 lobes ray-cast into one scalloped silhouette, painted as one light wet wash, then 3 clipped glaze tiers (mid, dark, under-crown band) with hard scalloped tops; leaf dabs break the outline; paper-white reserved leaves on the lit side; no decorative marks that could read as faces.
Tree palettes (light / mid / accent): #d9a443/#c26a31/#8a8a3a, #9aa648/#d0a046/#6f7f3a, #e08a3a/#b8452c/#d6aa4c, #c49a3e/#8f8a3a/#b5602e.
Plants sway with the wind: a shear from the base (trees 0.03, firs 0.018, reeds 0.075, bushes 0.022) driven by a slow travelling gust 0.55 + 0.45 sin(0.37 t + x * 0.004).
Every prop has its own indigo glaze shadow ellipse in the shared shadow path (tree 21x6.5, fir 13x4.5, bush 10x3.2, haystack 13x4, fence 16x2.6, wall 17x3, boulder 11x3.4, reeds 6x1.6 units).
Crowns fade to 42 % alpha while a character is behind them; props are y-sorted with characters and drawn as baked sprites.

effects.name: Impact
effects.how: Layered, 0.13-0.24 s: a blotted paper-white lift (core) snaps open, an ink splash sprite (wet pool with a dark pooled rim, 5-7 detached teardrops pointing outward, fine spatter) eases out, 4 paint drops fly along the knock direction and land as flattened stains; floating creatures add a rising grey-blue wisp.

effects.name: Dissolve
effects.how: The creature freezes in its hit pose and lifts to paper (first 18 % of 0.35 s), then 6 baked dissolve frames slump the wash (drips per column, base spreads 32 %) and bleed it out top-down while a puddle in its colours grows underneath; plus a bloom ring (1.1-1.5 s), a residue stain that dries for 1.8-2.4 s, 9-18 paint drops and torn leaves or wisps.

effects.name: Spawn
effects.how: A wet stain blooms first (ease-out, radius r*0.4 -> 1.6), the soft blurred copy rises out of it with a 12 % stretch and an 8 % overshoot, the crisp sprite and its ink fade in from 45 % of 0.45 s; the shadow grows in with it.

effects.name: Seed projectile
effects.how: A small cream seed wash with ink outline, spinning, preceded by an 18-unit dry-brush trail (tapered orange ribbon with streak gaps cut out); half the throws drop an orange paint fleck.

effects.name: Collectible twinkle and gold bloom
effects.how: Gold drops pop with an overshoot, large stars hover with an eased hold and flash a brush twinkle (four tapered ochre ticks + a paper dot) on their own timer; collecting adds ticks and gold drops, the gold bloom adds a gold backrun ring (40 units, 1.2 s) and 8 ticks around the character.

effects.name: Dash smear
effects.how: A 40 ms crouch (anticipation), then the stretched lunge with two fading wet copies 7 units apart, an indigo dry-brush smear, two umber dust puffs and 4 umber drops; a landing squash with overshoot follows.

effects.name: Lantern
effects.how: Orbiting carved root lanterns hang from a looped stalk and swing against the orbit (follow-through), casting a warm light pool on the ground.

effects.name: Floating counters
effects.how: Caveat 700, 10.5 px (accent 15 px, #9e2a1c on a faint red splash), paper-coloured 2.4-3 px stroke behind, rotated +-0.14 rad, pop-in scale 0.55 -> 1.15.

atmosphere.summary: No colour grading, bloom or vignette shader: light is painted into the washes (upper left), shadows are one indigo glaze, warm additive glows appear only on carved faces, cracks and lanterns, single leaves drift through the scene on the wind, and a deckled bare-paper page margin frames the screen.
rules: Light from the upper left (-0.6, -0.8): highlight blob at 30 %/26 % of each bbox, dark blob bottom-right, ink thicker on the shadow side.
Shadows: one union Path2D of ellipses offset (+0.8, +0.4) units, filled once per frame in rgba(50,54,92,0.2); floating subjects in a second path at 0.11. Never black or grey.

Glow sprite: radial rgba(255,226,140,.95) -> rgba(255,196,90,.5) at 35 % -> 0, composited lighter at 0.22-0.38 alpha with sine flicker (0.3 + 0.08 sin 11t + 0.05 sin 23t); lantern light pools on the ground at 0.55.

Ambient: world-anchored cells of 230 units, 5 of 8 hold one autumn leaf that falls from 74 units over 82 % of a 10-17 s period while drifting 52 units with the wind, tumbling edge-on, with its own soft shadow; trees, reeds and bushes shear in slow gusts.

Page margin (~2.4 % of height, corner radius 7 %): smoothstep paper fade (32 %), a sienna rim line rgb(120,82,58) at 22 % 3.5 units inside the edge, then opaque paper; the edge is perturbed into a torn deckle. Built once per screen size, drawn as 4 edge strips (11 % band).
Red edge tint: an alizarin wash rgb(178,44,34) replaces the margin and creeps in from the edges.
Night: darken with an indigo multiply glaze over the ground and keep the carved-glow light sources; never switch the ink to black.

ui.summary: HUD elements are painted wash strokes inside hand-inked frames on paper: an ochre wash bar across the top, a red wash bar with a ragged right edge and a heart icon, a feathered paper plaque behind the clock with an ink swash ornament, and deckle-edged paper cards (224x292, slightly rotated) for choice screens.

motion: Painted held poses, never tweened shapes: the main character walks on 8 baked poses at ~11 fps (distance-based, anim * 1.25), idles on 6 breathing poses held 0.42 s each (on twos), blinks every 3.9 s (a double blink every third time) and glances at the viewer for 1.2 s every 9.7 s.

Walk rig: body bob 0.75 * cos(2 * (ph - 0.35)), head 0.5 * cos(2 * (ph - 0.95)) (overlap), feet +-2.5 * cos(ph) with lift max(0, sin) * 2, hands counter-swing +-2.7, scarf tail as a travelling wave sin(2ph - 1.5); the pumpkin leaf flutters with it.

Dash: crouch frame for the first 40 ms (squash 1.08 x 0.9), stretch frame (1.1 x 0.94) for the lunge, landing squash with outBack overshoot over 150 ms. Flinch frame for the first 45 % of a hurt, with a paper-white lift.

Creatures: 6-pose cycles; small ~7 fps waddle (squash 5 % on each contact, rock +-0.085 rad, leaves lag 1.25 rad), fast ~4.5 fps (hem wave lags 1.3 / 2.6 rad, arms 0.9 rad, eased hover -2.4 + hover(2.7t) * 1.4), large ~3.3 fps heavy stomp (mass drops 2.1 units per contact, arms and leaf crown lag); phase, scale 0.93-1.07 and breathing rate per seed.
Hit: hit pose + 12 %/10 % squash against the knock for 140 ms, paper lift fading with the flash; death 0.35 s (freeze 18 %, then 6 bleed frames); spawn 0.45 s (stain, rise with overshoot, ink last).
Effects ease out: impact lift 0.13 s, splashes 0.24-0.36 s, bloom rings 1.1-1.5 s, paint drops 0.9-1.7 s with gravity 240-260, residue stains dry over 1.8-2.4 s.
Ambient motion is slower than any actor: wind gusts 0.37 rad/s, falling leaves on 10-17 s cycles, lantern flicker 11 / 23 rad/s.
do: Mix ground colour per pixel in absorbance space and darken wash edges (pooling, paper gaps).
Compose the ground: reeds and lily pads by water, litter and roots under trees, flowers in single-species drifts, tufts in clumps with calm paper between them.
Draw every coloured shape as wash first, ink second, with the wash offset ~0.45/0.35 units from the ink.
Build foliage as glazes: one light silhouette wash, then multiply tiers with hard scalloped edges on the shade side.
Pose characters with a rig (planted feet, lagging head, trailing cloth) and bake 6-8 poses per cycle; give every creature its own phase.
Layer every effect: paper-lift core, ink or paint splash, flying drops, residue that dries on the ground.
Bake all sprite frames once; per frame only drawImage. Frame the screen with a deckled bare-paper margin.
dont: Don't use hard flat fills with uniform black strokes (that turns it into cartoon vector art).
Don't use pure black or neutral grey: no #000 ink, no grey shadows.
Don't sprinkle tufts, flowers or dots evenly over the ground.
Don't paint tree crowns as rows of equal circles or decorate them with small marks that read as eyes.
Don't tween sprites with sine bobs instead of drawn poses, and don't let a crowd animate in sync.
Don't generate washes per frame with canvas blur filters: it costs milliseconds per sprite.
Don't use glowing circles as effects or saturated full-screen post effects; don't fill the paper margin with the world.
performance: Expensive at init (1-3 s): 6 noise textures (1024 px wash flow, 256 px paper/grain) by repeated box blur, ~60 character frames (rig poses, hit poses, flash, soft and dissolve copies), 28 prop sprites, FX sprites and HUD textures, each wash using canvas blur filters. Ground chunks (256 units, per-pixel shader + decals, up to 2.5 px/unit) are built by a generator that yields every 1-2 rows (5 ms budget per frame); pixels far from every wash edge skip pooling and gap maths and water terms are only evaluated near ponds, so a chunk costs about what the simpler original shader did. Per frame: chunk blits, one shadow Path2D fill, y-sorted sprite drawImage (wind sway as an exact shear and unshear, no save/restore), a few additive glows, ground stains, falling leaves and the cached page-margin strips. No per-frame filters or getImageData.
